item.name: The Best Watches of 2022… So Far.
item.author: Matthew Lopez
item.description: 2022 has been a record-breaking year in the world of fine watchmaking. From the much-anticipated release of the 50th-anniversary collection of the Royal Oak to the exciting novelties that were launched at Watches and Wonders, the world of watches has never been this exciting.

details.description: 2022 has been a record-breaking year in the world of fine watchmaking. From the much-anticipated release of the 50th-anniversary collection of the Royal Oak to the exciting novelties that were launched at Watches and Wonders, the world of watches has never been this exciting. But beyond all the social media hype, what timepieces truly were the diamonds in the rough? Today, we discuss what were the best watches released so far in 2022, and why you should not miss out on any of them.
Audemars Piguet Royal Oak “Jumbo” Extra-Thin “50th Anniversary” Ref. 16202

This year marked the 50th anniversary of the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, the first luxury sports watch made in stainless steel. To commemorate this important milestone, the brand under the leadership of its energetic CEO François-Henry Bennahmias in partnership with its Head of Complications Michael Friedman conceptualized an entirely new collection to pay a proper homage to the watch icon.

The new collection retained the design language of the discontinued Ref. 15202 kept in the same 39mm octagonal case. The specialists at Le Brassus developed the contemporary automatic caliber 7121, with a larger movement measuring a diameter of 29.6mm that encases 268 components at a higher frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour (VPH) and is tastefully decorated with a Côtes de Genève finishing.

Our personal favorite is the stainless steel model that now comes with a new dial color of bleu nuit, Nuage 50, that shifts color between black and blue. Friedman stated in a recent interview that this new color change was based on the original reference released in 1972 that in his view should be in trend to taste of the times without veering away from its origins. And because of this, the new Royal Oaks are must-haves on this year’s list.

No discussion about watches in 2022 would be complete without mentioning the collectability of the Cartier Crash. Originating from a timepiece that survived a car crash in 1967, the watch stands out as one of the most innovative designs of the 20th century. It has come to no surprise that Crash has gained a significant following in recent years with celebrities sporting it. Given its popularity, our next choice would be the limited edition, Crash Tigrée.

Inspired by tiger prints and textiles, the Crash Tigrée transforms this stylish watch into a fun fashionable accessory. To create this bejeweled object, the artisans at Cartier employed the usage of champlevé, an ancient enameling process where the designs are carved into a die and are later filled with liquid porcelain that when fired gives off a glossy texture. Back in April, at our special wrap-up episode on The Collector, Swiss collector Roy Davidoff talked about how it took their team over a hundred hours perfecting the design. And we couldn’t agree more with his sentiments, as this timepiece is a work of modern art on your wrist that anyone can wear.

Talking about the best watches of the year would not be right without talking about the high demand for sports watches. In recent years, there has been a growing resurgence towards them dominated primarily by the Royal Oak and the recently discontinued Patek Philippe Nautilus. But given that these timepieces have since become out of reach to many, other enthusiasts have been seeking the perfect alternative. Our pick would be one of the hottest releases this year, the rebirth of the legendary 222 by Vacheron Constantin.

First launched in 1977, the 222 was made to commemorate the 222nd anniversary of the brand’s founding. Designed by Jörg Hysek who would later become one of the most-sought-after watch designers in the industry, it was the culmination of Vacheron’s quest to produce its own integrated sports watch after numerous attempts in the past. Now relaunched as part of the Historiques collection, the new 222 comes in a 37mm yellow gold case with its match integrated bracelet and the signature Maltese cross on the 5 o’clock position. The watch has been upgraded to house the caliber 2455/2, an ultra-slim automatic movement that is more robust and easier to service.

Watch enthusiasts have been looking forward to the return of this classic for decades with everyone scrambling for an allocation. In our view, the new 222 can stand apart from its contemporaries as a leisurely sports watch that is both elegant and stylish on the wrist.

At the beginning of the year, many have been pondering the direction of the most venerable watch brand of them all, Patek Philippe. With the exponential growth that its sports watches have reached especially with the recent discontinuation of the Nautilus, some have argued for a return to its main forte, complications. Hence during the recent Watches and Wonders, Patek released its latest innovative timepiece in decades, the Annual Calendar Travel-Time.

In our introductory article last March, we profiled the new timepiece that combines two important and practical complications: the annual calendar and the travel time system for the display of a second-time zone. Here, you can switch the date and display immediately to synchronize it with the respective local time in your new destination.

What makes this timepiece remarkable is the fine details that the brand placed on its design elements by transforming the aesthetics of pilot’s watches from the 1940s, into a premier timepiece for the modern-day business traveler. And with the resumption of travel, this is sure to be a handy watch to have.

As demands for mainstream brands have been on the rise, certain collectors want to stand out by choosing lesser-known independent watchmakers that can distinguish them from their peers. Their choice is the works made by the French watchmaker, François-Paul Journe, who has become one of the vanguards of independent watchmaking. As the master approaches nearly 40 years in the business, he has begun redeveloping his earlier creations for the modern era. Now in 2022, he has brought back one of his cherished classics, the Vagabondage.

 

The Vagabondage is considered one of the most prized timepieces by collectors, given that Journe and his atelier have produced a very limited amount with a few examples rarely surfacing at auctions. Launched in 2004, the steampunk-inspired timepiece featured a wandering jump hour complication that surrounds an exposed balance wheel in the center. The revived model is based on the original design, but now features a slate grey outer dial and is encased in a fine 6N gold case.

 

 

Since its release, enthusiasts have been scrambling to get their hands on this piece, as the brand has prioritized giving the new model to those who bought the first Vagabondage eighteen years ago. It is no wonder that this oddity has become an object of fascination among collectors. And one can be sure that if an example were to surface under the hammer, it could even bring in a world record.

Always of the Highest Quality

Of the hundreds of watches we have seen and discussed in the past six months, only a few can be considered the best of them all. What we have mentioned in this article could be some of the top timepieces, others would say otherwise. But as we approach the mid-point of the year, more fascinating timepieces are set to come our way. Yet, one should remember that the best watches can be the true diamonds in the rough. These need not be the most popular ones on your Instagram feed, but all these timepieces are always of the highest quality, and it would be a big mistake to pass on them at all.
